pr_title: Prevent SignalR Hub from being cached from CDN on LongPolling
pr_body:
# Prevent SignalR Hub from being cached from CDN on LongPolling

Set the appropriate headers in the response to prevent caching.

Fixes #38437

issue_context.title: Prevent ASP.NET Core SignalR Hub from being cached from CDN on LongPolling
issue_context.body:
We have an application which exposes an endpoint which is an asp.net core signalr hub.

When testing on longpolling (mandatory) we found out erratic behaviour from the cdn (in this case, cloudfront) caching the responses the hub makes to the client.

Is there any way to add Cache-Control headers in LongPolling responses ? 

Reconfiguring cloudfront would not be an option, unfortunately.
comments: Triage: We will add the Cache-Control headers by default. @BrennanConroy  can you provide a workaround for this ?

Thank you for the quick response and workaround.

I saw this labeled for NET 7 planning and being this a best-practice on long polling (https://tools.ietf.org/id/draft-loreto-http-bidirectional-07.html#network) , what would be the chance for this (by default behaviour) to be added still on NET 6 roadmap (or even as an optional/opt-in feature?)

This is the first time we're seeing someone report this issue in the more than 4 years since releasing. Combined with the workaround it's unlikely we'll patch this at this point.
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/Servicing.md#servicing-bar

review_comments: I couldn't do the change to `CookieAuthenticationHandler` as a code fix, but I think we should do that too. I don't think we need the comment in `AddNoCacheHeaders` since we have this.
